method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

sourceChecks.authority: Health Canada with Canadian Paediatric Society and partner organizations
supports: 026 iron-rich complementary foods around six months
sourceChecks.scope: Specific infant-feeding claims; not validation of every item.

supports: 032 responsive interaction and ability to learn more than one language
sourceChecks.scope: Supports key and proposed language-restriction correction.
Vaccine-specific exceptions exist, including antibiotics with oral typhoid and nasal congestion affecting live intranasal delivery; revised065 should specify an injected non-live vaccine.

items.assessment: Developmental readiness and six-month timing support iron-rich complementary food alongside milk, not nutritionally weak replacement feeds.
Comfort with mashed texture supports supervised soft finger-food progression without waiting for molars or perfect utensil skill.
Avoiding honey before12months is correct; cereal thickening is a weak distractor unrelated to spores.
issues: Avoiding honey before12months is correct; cereal thickening is a weak distractor unrelated to spores.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Heat the honey at home before adding it. Explain that routine domestic heating does not reliably remove botulism spores; attach primary infant-feeding guidance.

items.assessment: Upright supervised stable feeding addresses movement-associated risk; texture/portion changes alone do not.
Turning away, closed mouth and satisfied relaxation support pause/stop; rooting supports interest. Foundation classification is appropriate.
Safe crib placement and short calming break directly address expressed escalating anger; safe surface matters.
Responsive family-language key is sound; restricting conversation to the nurses language is an artificial distractor.
issues: Responsive family-language key is sound; restricting conversation to the nurses language is an artificial distractor.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Use only one family language until first words develop. Explain that responsive multilingual interaction need not be restricted solely because more than one language is used.

items.assessment: Hearing/development assessment is sound; more background music is an implausible response.
issues: Hearing/development assessment is sound; more background music is an implausible response.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Speak more loudly and defer assessment while waiting for first words. Explain that altered speaking volume does not establish hearing ability and may delay early support.

items.assessment: Loss of established skills warrants prompt review; a language app then review next year is excessively delayed filler.
issues: Loss of established skills warrants prompt review; a language app then review next year is excessively delayed filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Ask the family to practise words for a month before arranging assessment. Explain that home practice can accompany, but should not postpone, evaluation of regression.

items.assessment: Trajectory, technique and feeding/health context appropriately interpret unexpected weight; sibling weight is a recognizable comparison error.
Corrected age and progress contextualize preterm development; cousin comparison and hospital duration are insufficient.
Caregiver-held gradual approach fits nonurgent assessment and age-typical stranger distress; no claim that distress proves disorder.
Painless chalky tooth change warrants early dental review; excessive brushing pressure or waiting for permanent teeth is inappropriate.
Practice followed by adult assistance balances skill development with effective cleaning of missed surfaces.
Regular nutritious choices with child appetite-based amount form responsive toddler structure; clean-plate coercion does not.
Strong resistance and absent signalling support readiness-based pause rather than forced sitting/fluid restriction.
Two acceptable shirts provide bounded autonomy within necessary routine; broad yes/no task choice is a meaningful contrast.
Correct preparation is defensible, but starting explanations weeks ahead is temporally impossible for a draw scheduled later today.
issues: Correct preparation is defensible, but starting explanations weeks ahead is temporally impossible for a draw scheduled later today.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Use a detailed diagram of the circulation to explain the blood tests. Replace option2 with: Repeat the full procedure explanation throughout the day until the child can recite each step. Explain developmentally concrete, brief, near-term preparation.

items.assessment: Key correctly addresses magical thinking, but all alternatives endorse blame or causation unrealistically.
issues: Key correctly addresses magical thinking, but all alternatives endorse blame or causation unrealistically.
proposedChanges: Use distractors: Tell the child angry feelings are normal, then change the subject; Explain the disease mechanism using detailed medical terms; Invite the child to help care for the brother as a way to make amends. Explain why these fail to directly correct false causation or reinforce guilt.

items.assessment: Concrete cause/effect, supervised practice and shared manageable tasks support school-age self-care without sole refill responsibility.
All wrong options are extreme/irrelevant (permanent school removal, withheld rewards, supplements only).
issues: All wrong options are extreme/irrelevant (permanent school removal, withheld rewards, supplements only).
proposedChanges: Replace alternatives with: Review breakfast foods as the only focus; Start an attendance-reward plan before hearing the child perspective; Ask the parent about school while excluding the child account. Explain that contextual child-centred assessment follows reassuring initial review while remaining open to clinical changes.

items.assessment: Routine screen-free intervention is sound; screen size is irrelevant filler.
issues: Routine screen-free intervention is sound; screen size is irrelevant filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with: Move the device to the living room while keeping the same meal and bedtime viewing schedule. Explain that location alone does not address displacement at those routines.

items.assessment: Free enjoyable movement addresses cost barrier without equating activity with competitive organized sport.
Nonstigmatizing growth/routine assessment addresses distress while avoiding unassessed rapid restriction or appearance-based goals.
Private puberty guidance about variation, practical questions and trusted resources is defensible; classmates alone do not set an individual standard.
Private opportunity and confidentiality limits are appropriate; parent guessing answers is implausible nursing practice.
issues: Private opportunity and confidentiality limits are appropriate; parent guessing answers is implausible nursing practice.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Ask the teenager and parent to complete the sensitive-topic questionnaire together. Explain that a jointly completed form does not provide a confidential opportunity to speak.

items.assessment: Practices/protection assessment avoids identity-based risk assumption and supports individualized prevention.
Asymptomatic infection possibility supports exposure/guidance-based screening without equating pregnancy prevention with STI testing.
Separate pregnancy/infection prevention key is sound; stopping contraception before discussing risk is unrelated filler.
issues: Separate pregnancy/infection prevention key is sound; stopping contraception before discussing risk is unrelated filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option2 with: Delay condom discussion until the next device replacement visit. Explain that current new exposure warrants prevention discussion now, independent of device schedule.

items.assessment: Supported condition explanation, booking and refill planning build gradual transition rather than abrupt task transfer.
Heavy bleeding with fatigue and school impairment warrants severity/anemia review beyond normalizing adolescent variability.
Energy/overall-health assessment is correct; more training and race-results tracking are implausible clinical alternatives.
issues: Energy/overall-health assessment is correct; more training and race-results tracking are implausible clinical alternatives.
proposedChanges: Replace option0 with: Prioritize calcium supplementation without reviewing total energy intake. Replace option3 with: Discuss medication to produce regular bleeding before evaluating the change. Explain that these can miss underlying low energy availability and broader differential assessment.

items.assessment: Dependence and stress-function exploration with cessation support responds to nicotine use without presenting smoking comparison as permission to start vaping.
Base-tan misconception is appropriately corrected with multiple ultraviolet protection strategies.
Consistent wake time, reduced bedtime stimulation and wind-down support sleep; energy drinks do not replace lost sleep.
Screening versus diagnosis distinction is correct; absence of symptoms cannot prove abnormal result false. Mainly foundation-level knowledge.
New persistent rectal bleeding requires symptom assessment independent of prior routine screening interval.
Early cancer pattern in close relatives merits individualized risk assessment rather than automatic average-risk age rules or unselected markers.
Benefits, harms, follow-up and values support informed screening choice; selective fear/benefit framing does not.
Clinically correct but repeats predictable three-good/one-obvious-bad SATA pattern and booked-dose/age-only option is very weak.
issues: Clinically correct but repeats predictable three-good/one-obvious-bad SATA pattern and booked-dose/age-only option is very weak.
proposedChanges: Recast as findings needing clarification before vaccination, with two positive answers among five: prior anaphylaxis to same product and currently significant febrile illness; nonkeys may be brief prior local soreness, mild afebrile rhinorrhea, antibiotic use alone without relevant illness. Verify vaccine-specific details and keep wording assessment-focused rather than declaring universal contraindications.

items.assessment: Mild afebrile rhinitis alone generally does not defer vaccination; current vaccine-specific assessment avoids overgeneralization.
Available records and individualized catch-up assessment avoid indefinite delay or unselected restart assumptions.
Clarifying local soreness versus severe allergy is sound; leftover antibiotics before vaccines is cartoon unsafe.
issues: Clarifying local soreness versus severe allergy is sound; leftover antibiotics before vaccines is cartoon unsafe.
proposedChanges: Replace option3 with: Premedicate with an antihistamine before every future vaccine without further assessment. Explain that routine premedication does not establish a true allergy or replace reaction-specific assessment.

items.assessment: Early itinerary/chronic-medication review is sound; tourism rating and antibiotics for every possible illness are filler.
issues: Early itinerary/chronic-medication review is sound; tourism rating and antibiotics for every possible illness are filler.
proposedChanges: Replace option1 with: Focus only on travel vaccines without reviewing chronic medication supply. Replace option2 with: Base advice on the destination country alone without itinerary or accommodation details. Explain that individual health, routes, activities and practical medication planning influence preparation.

items.assessment: Age/dose history, conditions and exposure risks inform adult vaccination; a single childhood dose is not evidence of complete protection.

batchNote: SATA items occur every fifth ID and almost all have exactly first three choices keyed with one obvious nonkey. Vary context, option count, correct count and position across future batches; current editorial passes are not psychometric validation. Final source registry still needs item-specific claims distinguished from general reading.
